scope: Proposition 4.1 of the manuscript “Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing” (preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 118 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cf1e9b383ad38a1c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: If the input graph has a vertex cover of size at most k, the constructed items can be packed into B bins.
